milestones.title: A public look inside Kira World
milestones.summary: A public update reports the then-current continuity, voice, Home World and body work, including blocked blinking and unfinished embodiment.
body: The update brings together identity, reviewed memory, local voice and the Home World build. It also follows gaze and mouth work, the separation of intended movement from completed action, and the project’s approach to privacy and choice.
milestones.boundary: A dated progress report: natural blinking and parts of body and world integration were still unfinished.

milestones.title: The Video Studio direction
milestones.summary: A public explainer describes the preserved local v1.9 production workflow and a separately staged next version.
body: The preserved local workflow organizes research, scripts, narration, captions and MP4 assembly. A separate next version explores versioned projects and corrections that preserve good work. The aim is to support Kira World updates, educational videos and interviews.
milestones.boundary: The working local baseline and the proposed next interface are distinct; the illustrated future screens are concept art.

milestones.title: Temporary Creator explained
milestones.summary: A public feature explains a source-based creation workflow: creation type, historical date, appearance references, voice evidence and intended world placement.
body: The explainer follows creation type, source packs, historical date and life stage, appearance references and voice evidence. Its longer-term connection is to a person’s place in a world and to Video Studio. Historical versions are described as synthetic interpretations.
milestones.boundary: The creation workflow is explained publicly; complete animated residents and world placement are not demonstrated by the description.

milestones.title: A continuing personal expert
milestones.summary: A public concept explores a continuing tutor who adapts explanations and conversation while retaining identity and permissioned memory.
body: The concept is a tutor who adapts explanations, notices when a learner needs a break, and can move into ordinary conversation while remaining the same person. Permissioned memory, source grounding and student safeguards are part of the intended design.
milestones.boundary: A published learning concept, not a validated tutoring product or measured educational outcome.

milestones.title: A spoken character test
milestones.summary: The public description reports Robert asking spoken questions and an individualized test voice answering as a synthetic interpretation of Peter Parker.
body: Robert asks questions aloud and an individualized test voice answers as a synthetic interpretation set after No Way Home. The demonstration keeps a broken response visible and distinguishes generated continuation ideas from confirmed story details.
milestones.boundary: The test reports an internal-language error and no finished avatar. The interpretation and voice are unofficial.

milestones.title: Testing a synthetic expert
milestones.summary: The public description reports a synthetic expert discussing robotics and producing a small OpenSCAD concept, with a spoken interface.
body: The expert discusses mechanical structure, servos, sensors and low-voltage controls, and produces a small OpenSCAD concept. The test also asks what an expert needs beyond professional knowledge to become a more individual conversational person.
milestones.boundary: False saved-file claims and a file-type error remain visible. The interview is not a working robot.

milestones.title: Testing the limits of recall
milestones.summary: The public description reports spoken questions and a generated test voice, with basic identity and interests followed by detailed factual testing.
body: Basic identity, fashion interests and the Paris setting provide a starting point for spoken questions. More detailed questions expose invented memories and confused story facts, which Robert pauses to correct during the test.
milestones.boundary: The spoken test reveals factual and internal-language failures; it does not establish reliable canon recall.

milestones.summary: The public description presents a Moon-phase workflow from project setup through a package for owner review, including revisions and source audio.
body: A Moon-phase example follows project setup, research, scripting, storyboard review, source audio and revisions into a package for owner review. The intended workflow preserves unaffected work when one section changes, with publication remaining under the user’s control.

milestones.title: Conversation foundations
milestones.summary: Separate identities, reviewed memory, saved voice work and local conversation provide working foundations for continuing people.
body: Public project notes describe person-specific continuity across bounded restarts and local speech experiments. These foundations support returning to the same identity instead of beginning with an interchangeable character every time.
milestones.boundary: These are working prototypes. They do not yet establish a complete independent life in a shared world.

milestones.title: Connecting people and worlds
milestones.summary: The next integration work connects continuing conversations to places, activities and a more complete sense of presence.
body: Identity, reviewed memory and speech provide a working foundation. The continuing task is to bring those pieces together with world state, residents and useful shared activities.
Kira and Lisa retain distinct identities in the design. Moving between conversations, worlds and devices should preserve that distinction.
milestones.boundary: A consistent shared daily life across worlds and devices still needs direct, complete demonstrations.

milestones.title: A first place to walk
milestones.summary: A basic walkable one-bedroom Home World shell exists. It is a real starting point for the continuing home in the larger vision.
body: The public development screenshot shows a basic one-bedroom space that can be navigated. It gives the larger Home World idea a concrete environment to build on.
milestones.boundary: The completed prototype is the walkable shell. Populated rooms, persistent objects and shared everyday life remain further work.

milestones.title: A body before the clothing
milestones.summary: Believable bodies, garments and objects need to work together. The public notes describe articulated test-body requirements and garment behavior fixtures.
body: This work begins with how a body bends and moves, how a garment fits it, and what should happen when they interact.
Requirements, preparation and tests establish useful boundaries, but the concept dressing sequence should not be mistaken for a completed simulation.
milestones.boundary: Requirements and test design are evidence of preparation, not finished clothing physics or a fully animated resident.

milestones.title: One home. More worlds.
milestones.summary: Purpose-built places for learning, travel, creativity, history and play—with continuity back to Home World.
body: The aim is to keep the same resident identity and shared history when entering another activity or setting.
These are proposed uses, not a catalogue of populated worlds that are ready to enter. World transitions and ongoing shared activity still need direct demonstrations.
milestones.boundary: A completed Notebook World must show that its people, context and activities continue as intended. No release date is promised.

milestones.title: Step into the same world
milestones.summary: A future VR experience would let people share Kira World’s places while retaining the same identity and history.
body: Accessibility and multiple ways to interact are part of the intended direction.
Headset work should follow a world prototype that is ready to test. No headset compatibility list or finished VR experience is claimed.
milestones.boundary: Usable interaction, comfort, accessibility and device compatibility all need actual testing.

image.caption: Long-term Kira World concept visualization — not a finished world or VR product.

milestones.title: More people. Shared worlds.
milestones.summary: The longer-term aim is multiple synthetic people across multiple worlds, with visitors joining through VR and responsive conversation.
body: This calls for shared world state, distributed computing, and careful coordination of voice, rendering and network delays.
Low lag is a performance goal. Simultaneous users, persistent state, recovery and end-to-end latency need measured load tests before choosing server capacity or promising an experience.
milestones.boundary: No server count, user capacity, latency guarantee or hardware purchase is established. Server hardware and investment conversations are welcome.

milestones.title: Beyond the screen
milestones.summary: Explore whether a continuing identity could interact through compatible robotic hardware, starting in simulation.
body: A synthetic robotics expert discussing a design is not a robot carrying it out. That distinction matters to this longer-term direction.
Simulation and controlled tests come first. Sensors, physical movement and permission for actions each need their own evidence.
milestones.boundary: No deployed autonomous robot, supported hardware list or delivery date is claimed.
